title: Learning Plan
description: Canonical data model for a learning-planner-skill roadmap. This file is the single source of truth from which the Detailed Learning Plan (learning-plan.md) and the Dashboard (dashboard.md / Notion export) are generated by scripts/render_plan.py and scripts/render_dashboard.py.

modules.description: Flat list of all modules and submodules. Hierarchy is expressed via parent_id; learning order/dependencies are expressed via prerequisites. A flat list (rather than nested submodule arrays) keeps graph algorithms (cycle detection, availability computation) simple for scripts.

title.description: Title of the overall roadmap, e.g. 'Mastering Distributed Systems'.

discipline.description: The subject/discipline, e.g. 'Distributed Systems', 'Classical Guitar', 'Category Theory', 'Constitutional Law'.

goal_type.description: Primary learning-goal type driving emphasis. 'mastery' = broad mastery-oriented (Use Case 1/5), 'research' = research-level depth (Use Case 2), 'career' = role-capability oriented (Use Case 3), 'exam-prep' = deadline/exam-driven (Use Case 4), 'general' = doesn't fit the above cleanly.

target_outcome.description: What success looks like, in the user's own words.

current_level.description: User's starting point/background, used for scoping and gap analysis.

timeline.description: Free-text timeline or deadline, e.g. '3 months', 'no fixed deadline', 'before finals on 2026-09-01'.

id.description: Unique slug for this module, e.g. 'consensus-algorithms'. Used as the reference target for parent_id and prerequisites.

parent_id.description: ID of the parent module if this is a submodule; null for top-level modules.

category.description: Primary classification: core = required for the stated goal, optional = enriches but isn't required, advanced = beyond the core mastery bar (extension/frontier material).

sequencing.description: Whether this module must be completed in order relative to its sibling modules (sequential), or can be studied alongside them (parallel).

skippable.description: Whether a learner with relevant prior experience may skip this module after a lightweight validation (relevant to skill-gap-analysis use case).

prerequisites.description: IDs of modules that must reach status 'completed' before this module becomes 'available'. May reference modules anywhere in the flat list, regardless of parent_id hierarchy.

estimated_effort.description: Free-text effort estimate, e.g. '1 week', '10-15 hours', '2-3 sessions'. Left as free text since units vary by discipline and pace.

status.description: 'locked' and 'available' are computed by scripts/update_progress.py from prerequisites; 'in-progress' and 'completed' are set by the user via the same script. Maps directly to the Dashboard's Kanban columns (locked=Blocked, available=Not Started, in-progress=In Progress, completed=Completed).

is_milestone.description: Marks capstone/checkpoint modules (e.g. a milestone project) for the Dashboard's Milestones view.

learning_objectives.description: What the learner should be able to do after completing this module.

deep_understanding_concepts.description: Concepts within this module that require genuine depth, not surface familiarity -- the ideas where shortcuts cause downstream problems.

common_mistakes.description: Mistakes or misconceptions learners typically have at this stage.

expected_competence.description: The bar for considering this module genuinely 'done' -- described concretely enough to self-assess against.

industry_expectations.description: What practitioners, employers, or the field at large expect at this level. May be an empty string if not meaningfully applicable to this module.

mastery_goals.description: Longer-horizon goals this module contributes to (may span beyond the module itself).

method.description: Free-text evaluation method, adapted to the discipline -- e.g. 'project', 'proof', 'derivation', 'debugging exercise', 'performance recording', 'case study', 'literature review', 'oral explanation'. See references/domain-evaluation-guide.md for selecting appropriate methods; this is intentionally not an enum.

description.description: Concrete description of the evaluation task for this module.

real_world_competence.description: Troubleshooting scenarios, edge cases, trade-offs, or practical/industry constraints relevant to this module.

title.description: Resource name if source is 'user-provided', or a description of what's needed if source is 'needed'.

source.description: 'needed' marks an explicitly flagged gap. Never invent a title for a 'needed' resource -- describe what's needed and ask the user to supply it.

notes.description: Any other context worth preserving for this module (optional).
